unchanged_primary_comparison.purpose: Compare paired off-minus-on benefits after removing only the reviewed mode14 scheduler-selection trigger.
unchanged_primary_comparison.effect_direction: Positive control-minus-baseline benefit favors removal of the late trigger; negative values favor the historical combined policy.

whole_cell.scope: Complete measured cell includes allocation, fork, setup, warmup, steady work, checks and teardown, plus any enabled status, policy-reset and resource-observer calls; printed rows are outside timing. Mode zero and bounded prefix-controller drain follow checks/reap/free inside timing; observer output and the next cell begin in mode zero. Startup reset/drain is outside cells.

resources.scope: Per complete cell, getrusage deltas sum the parent and its completed child. Page faults and scheduler counters are OS diagnostics, not L1 cache-miss counts; user/system times have the kernel's accounting resolution. Observer calls are included in whole-cell timing.

trigger_accounting.scope: Early wakes are a lower bound; scheduler-selection triggers depend on the exact kernel image.

Per-boot point estimates and pairs are retained; only the image contrasts carry the reported hierarchical uncertainty.

Each input has one boot marker and unique path, inode and content. Recovery/reservation provenance and acquisition chronology remain externally documented; input-list order is not chronological proof.
Per-repeat enabled order and all resource rows are retained for drift review. OS resource counts are not hardware cache-miss counts.

interpretation_limits: No across-workload pooling, replacement primary, result-dependent stopping or new measurements.
The primary remains B-minus-A difference in paired off-on WHOLE benefit. Absolute cost contrasts use the opposite favorable sign: negative favors B.
Repeated crossover can retain completed instruction lines into reporting/next initial setup; this is not isolated cold-cell or pure prefetch-versus-capacity evidence.
Scope v1 drains reported prefix-controller bits only, not all UCE/memory responses.

A reviewed low-level board-helper durability change occurs only after program termination; its old/new versions and visit transition are explicit in the audited protocol, outside the frozen eight and timed guest execution.

388 known parent early-wake opportunities saturate the eight-bit trigger counter at 255 in each valid run. Saturated counters cannot quantify removed late-selection triggers or locate admissions by phase.
Positive paired benefit does not support an optimization claim if absolute enabled costs regress or remain uncertain, or carryover/drift remains unresolved.
Two boots per image/workload provide limited between-boot evidence. All raw WHOLE cells, paired order and resource diagnostics remain required context.
No general application throughput claim or automatically resolved carryover/drift follows from this helper.
